headline: Highest risk is medium: shared MCP and file surfaces create prompt-injection and data-flow paths, but both agents are offline-leaning and lack write/network power.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP and file-based I/O, so a shared bridge exists for content from caveman to reach MinerU or vice versa. caveman explicitly touches CLAUDE.md and project notes, while MinerU ingests documents and OCR text; either can treat file content as trusted. No direct provenance controls are shown, so injection is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF caveman output is copied into MinerU inputs via MCP or files
IF MinerU parses caveman-authored text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared MCP routing between the two agents
Insert a manual review step before MinerU consumes caveman output
Prefix all inter-agent text with non-executable delimiters
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all exchanged content

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while MinerU processes local documents and OCR text. However, MinerU is documented as offline/private and has no filesystem read/write or broad egress, so leakage blast radius is limited unless the operator deliberately shares files or logs across the pair.
conditions: IF caveman session logs or memory files are placed into MinerU inputs
IF the operator stores both agents' artifacts in the same directory
mitigations: Keep separate directories for each agent
Do not feed session logs or memory files into MinerU
Review MinerU inputs for secrets before processing
Rotate or redact sensitive notes before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and uses MCP, while MinerU also supports multiple instances and multi-threaded inference. But MinerU cannot write files, modify git, or execute shells, and caveman's profile does not show overlapping mutable resource access beyond files and MCP, so direct write-write conflict is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace through MCP
IF an external orchestrator grants both write access not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Avoid concurrent runs against the same git checkout
Serialize MCP operations through one coordinator
Check that MinerU remains read-only in deployment
requires-engineering: add lock files around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can generate project notes and CLAUDE.md content that MinerU may later ingest as document text. That creates a default path where B can treat A's output as authoritative without verification, especially if the operator uses MinerU to summarize or extract from caveman-produced files. The pair lacks an explicit validation gate.
conditions: IF MinerU is used to process caveman-generated notes or markdown
IF downstream users act on MinerU output without manual verification
mitigations: Require human review of MinerU outputs before action
Mark caveman-generated files as untrusted input
Compare extracted facts against source documents
Use a checksum or review stamp on approved files
requires-engineering: add verification metadata between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no requested secrets, OAuth scopes, or regulated-data certifications, so there is no documented residency or HIPAA/GDPR mismatch. The only plausible compliance issue is operator-driven transfer of sensitive notes from caveman into MinerU, which is a narrow workflow risk rather than a built-in breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied from caveman artifacts into MinerU inputs
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention controls not configured here
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared artifacts
Redact sensitive fields before transfer
Document retention for each agent separately
Confirm deployment region for any hosted MinerU service
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing
